summary.plain: UA1 reported four electron-positron pairs and one muon pair whose combined mass, about 95 GeV/c², is the signature of a two-body decay of a heavy particle, which the paper reads as the neutral Z boson. CERN announced the discovery of the Z boson on 1 June 1983, after the W announcement of 25 January.
summary.technical: UA1 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 126 (1983) 398: four e+e- pairs and one mu+mu- pair with the signature of a two-body decay of a particle of mass ~95 GeV/c^2; the events fit well the hypothesis p-pbar -> Z0 + X with Z0 -> l+ l-, where Z0 is the Intermediate Vector Boson postulated by the electroweak theories as the mediator of weak neutral currents.

title: Experimental Observation of Lepton Pairs of Invariant Mass Around 95 GeV/c^2 at the CERN SPS Collider
why_it_matters: The paper identifies the Z0 as the Intermediate Vector Boson postulated by the electroweak theories as the mediator of weak neutral currents, and CERN announced the discovery of the Z boson on 1 June 1983, after the W announcement of 25 January 1983.
